variants.answer: I’d make replay an explicit, bounded operation rather than simply resetting a consumer group. I’d use immutable event IDs and partner/source metadata, then write processed IDs to an idempotency store so replays can’t duplicate downstream effects. I’d define replay by topic, partition, and offset or event-time range, run it first in a shadow consumer, and compare counts and outputs before enabling writes. In one fictional project, that approach cut duplicate records during backfills from 1.8% to under 0.1%, while keeping normal consumer lag below our alert threshold. I’d also preserve original timestamps, track replay jobs separately, and provide pause, rate-limit, and rollback controls.

variants.answer: I’d use idempotent processing, keep enough event history to support the replay window, and make replay ranges explicit. I’d also monitor lag and errors, and test a replay in a separate consumer group before applying it to production. That should reduce duplicate side effects and make failures easier to investigate.
